variants.headline: Builder left unpaid for work done
variants.sub: The builder {builder} is owed payment by the client {client} for completed work.
variants.body:
The client {client} has not paid the builder {builder} for work done. The amount owed is {owed}. After three missed months the builder stops work. For {target}, the event raises the basic question of responsibility when a construction undertaking requires payment as well as performance.

The gazette records the missed payment and the amount owed. The rule governing a stop after three missed months is distinct from an announcement that work has already stopped. An orderly account should preserve the difference between a current arrear and the condition under which further action follows.

The conduct of {target} merits scrutiny against the unpaid work. This account records the amount owed and the stopping rule without presuming that the current failure has already reached that rule's threshold. Care in the public record is part of responsible administration.

variants.headline: A construction payment fails to arrive
variants.sub: Payment for work done by {builder} has been missed by {client}.
variants.body:

An orderly account should preserve the difference between a current arrear and the condition under which further action follows.

variants.headline: Work delivered, payment outstanding
variants.sub: The client {client} has not paid {builder} for building work done.
variants.body:

The gazette records the missed payment and the amount owed. The rule governing a stop after three missed months is distinct from an announcement that work has already stopped. An orderly account should preserve the difference between a current arrear and the condition under which further action follows.
